import itertools

def get_h_s(S, n):
    H_S = []
    for i in range(1 << n):
        t = set()
        for j in range(n):
            if (i >> j) & 1:
                t.add(j)
        if all(t.intersection(s) for s in S):
            H_S.append(t)
    return H_S

def solve_n(n):
    max_2N = 0
    # To make it faster, we can't iterate over all S.
    # But we can iterate over some S.
    # For example, S can be a subset of the power set.
    # Since we want to maximize |S| and |H(S) \ S|, we can try different S.
    
    import random
    for _ in range(10000):
        # Try a random S size
        S_size = random.randint(1, 1 << (n-1))
        S = []
        all_subsets = []
        for i in range(1 << n):
            s = set()
            for j in range(n):
                if (i >> j) & 1:
                    s.add(j)
            all_subsets.append(s)
        
        S = random.sample(all_subsets, S_size)
        H_S = get_h_s(S, n)
        
        S_sets = set(tuple(sorted(list(s))) for s in S)
        H_S_filtered = [t for t in H_S if tuple(sorted(list(t))) not in S_sets]
        
        # We can pick |S|=N and |T|=N if min(|S|, |H_S_filtered|) >= N.
        # So for this S, we can have N = min(|S|, |H_S_filtered|).
        # Then 2N = 2 * min(|S|, |H_S_filtered|).
        max_2N = max(max_2N, 2 * min(len(S), len(H_S_filtered)))
        
    return max_2N

for n in range(3, 7):
    print(f"n={n}, max_2N={solve_n(n)}")
